customer_name: Quanzhou Water Group (泉州水务集团)
business_problem: Quanzhou Water Group needed to modernize complex water production, pumping, and distributed wastewater operations because traditional methods could not cope with rising demand for energy efficiency, leakage control, service quality, flood response, and broad asset visibility.
solution_summary: Baidu AI Cloud and partner Eredi built a 'Water Brain' operating model for Quanzhou Water Group that connects plant automation, pump-station scheduling, and distributed wastewater operations. In the Jinji water plant, smart-vision technology and intelligent applications monitor production lines, detect equipment anomalies, identify risky worker actions, and alert on abnormal temperature or vibration so two operators in a control room can manage processes that once required many more staff. For pressurized water-supply stations, an AI demand-forecasting model combines historical consumption data with weather, holidays, and seasonal changes to predict water use at more than 99% accuracy and dynamically adjust outlet pressure, pump flow, pressure, and frequency for demand-based supply. The same 'Water Brain' reduces field-inspection frequency for stable wastewater sites, converts paper巡检 into digital forms, and supports remote control when faults occur. A five-platform stack across big data, digital twins, command, operations, and public service turns the utility into a coordinated, analytics-driven water operator rather than a collection of manual systems.

solution_components.name: BML Full-Function AI Development Platform
solution_components.role: Provides the AI-development foundation behind Quanzhou Water Group's intelligent visual monitoring and predictive scheduling capabilities.

solution_components.name: Water Brain
solution_components.role: Coordinates plant automation, water-demand forecasting, wastewater operations, digital twins, and management applications across the water utility.

data_flow: Operational data from plants, pump stations, wastewater sites, and utility systems flows into the Water Brain, AI models forecast demand and detect anomalies, digital applications adjust pump parameters and dispatch operations, and managers consume the results through unified control, service, and visualization platforms.
business_outcome: Quanzhou Water Group improved staffing efficiency, lowered energy consumption, stabilized wastewater operations, and created a reusable intelligent-utility model for production, service, and environmental governance.
metrics: overall staff efficiency improved by more than 5%
architecture_clues: The utility uses smart vision, AI demand forecasting, digital twins, and remote-control workflows in one operating stack.
Stable wastewater sites can move from daily inspection to weekly inspection under the new model.
The platform includes a big-data layer and a digital-twin layer, not just point AI applications.
